actions-list.actionItem: Pursuant to the order of yesterday, the Journal of the proceedings of the Senate was deemed approved to date.
Pursuant to the order of yesterday,the morning hour being deemed expired, and the times for the recognition of the two leaders being reserved.
The following transactions of morning business occurred on today.

H.R. 2347 (Rep. Smucker):
        A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any damages, other than punitive damages, received on account of any sexual acts or sexual contact.

        -- Considered by Senate.
 

 S.Amdt. 6883 (Sen. Capito):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Considered by Senate.


 S.Amdt. 6884 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.


 S.Amdt. 6885 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.


 S.Amdt. 6886 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.


 S.Amdt. 6887 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Considered by Senate.




 H.R. 5254 (Rep. Bell):
        A bill to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to enter into an agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to host private events in Gateway Arch National Park buildings, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 H.R. 8454 (Rep. McClintock):
        A bill to provide for the transfer of administrative jurisdiction over certain Federal land in the State of California, and for other purposes.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 908 (Sen. Klobuchar):
        A resolution supporting the designation of the week of September 21 through September 25, 2026, as "National Hazing Awareness Week".

        -- Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 949 (Sen. Baldwin):
        A resolution designating October 12, 2026, as "National Loggers Day".

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 959 (Sen. Capito):
        A resolution recognizing the death of John Davison"Jay" Rockefeller IV, former Senator for the State of West Virginia.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.

PN1181-7:
        Anna St. John, of Louisiana, to be United States Circuit Judge for the Fifth Circuit

        -- Considered by Senate.

        -- Confirmed by the Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 52 - 46. Record Vote Number: 265
By unanimous consent, on the request of Mr. Husted, at  6:08 p.m., the Senate adjourned, under its order of today, until 10 a.m. tomorrow.
